recorded: Every case passed against the original with Python 3.15.2 and requests 2.34.2, run as python3 {program}.py, and with Node.js 26.12.1 and Danger JS 11.3.1, the version the template's workflow step names, run as npx danger ci --text-only --failOnErrors --dangerfile {program}.js, the command of the lesson's routewise-danger-demo pipeline, with one shell command choosing between them by {program}. No GitHub token was available, so every GitHub REST API response is synthesized from GitHub's documented format, for pull requests of unipds-engenharia-de-ia-aplicada/routewise-danger-demo: 42 and 43 carry pr-mock-routewise.json and pr-mock-falhas.json, and 44 to 46 cover the edges the mocks leave out. The cases set the variables of a GitHub Actions run for a pull_request event, point GITHUB_API_URL and DANGER_GITHUB_API_BASE_URL to the replay, and seed the event file, the coverage files, and the mocks. The Python original always calls https://api.github.com, so the copy that produced these cases reads GITHUB_API_URL first and falls back to that address, a one-line change. Danger JS asks for the pull request and for its diff at the same path, told apart by the Accept header, and every request it makes is incidental, so a Danger port or a Danger JS process may ask in its own order. The Dangerfile is checked by whether the run fails and by the report Danger JS prints, every failure, warning, and message in its section and order, skipping the summary line above it. The Python check is compared exactly, its GitHub requests in order with the comment it posts, except the hint after missing variables, which names the command that runs the local mode. A coverage of 79.25 shows that the Dangerfile rounds exact ties up and the Python check rounds them to even.
